509: QHA is far off for alloy cells. Measuring QHA − TI on the same cells gives −2 to −13 meV/atom at the pure-element ends, but −33 to −45 at x = 0.25 / 0.75 of Ag–Cu and up to −65 meV/atom for the fcc-Ni alloy and B2 defect cells of Ni–Al. When QHA-only cells without TI remain they pull the phase curves down, producing alternating fcc+fcc and fcc+liquid bands in Ag–Cu and, for SevenNet-0 Ni–Al, an fccAl+liquid band extending to 2000 K. The assembly therefore drops the QHA of those cells (qha_excluded: inside the Ag–Cu gap, dilute fcc-Al of Ni–Al).

514: 5. Point-defect model: from constitutional to thermal defects (04A)
515: The composition width of an ordered phase is set by the free energy of the point defects (anti-sites, vacancies) that carry the deviation from stoichiometry. ftphase can now treat this in two stages.
519: Only one kind per composition: anti-sites (both sides) for B32; for B2 NiAl, Ni anti-sites on the Ni side and Ni vacancies on the Al side (triple-defect-type constitution). `b32_antisite_site_fractions`, `b2_triple_defect_site_fractions`
520: Up to 4 kinds simultaneously: B anti-sites and vacancies on the A sublattice, A anti-sites and vacancies on the B sublattice. `wagner_schottky_free_energy`
522: Determined uniquely from the composition x (solving Eq. (E11) backwards)
523: For each (x, T), minimise G/atom = [(a+b) g₀ + Σ n_s y_d ε_d − T S_conf(y)] / N_atoms(y) under the composition constraint. The constraint is linear in y, so one variable is eliminated and the rest is minimised in log space (a one-dimensional bounded search when 2 defect kinds are allowed)
525: Eqs. (E10)–(E12) separated analytically and excluded from the fit
526: Same Eq. (E10). Evaluated inside the minimisation
528: Linear fit (slope) of the sample-cell G(x) per branch on either side of the stoichiometric composition
529: Directly from the sample cells at each temperature: ε_d(T) = (G_cell·N_atoms − g₀·N_sites) / n_defects, least-squares averaged per defect kind (`defect_energies_from_cells`, which recovers the defect kind and count from the cell's x and atom count). Since the QHA/TI G is used, this is an "effective" defect free energy including the vibrational contribution

532: G is smooth thanks to thermal defect pairs (B2: triple defect of 2 Ni vacancies + 1 Ni anti-site, B32: anti-site pairs). Reduces to the constitutional-defect model as T → 0
534: `entropy_models={"B2": ("wagner_schottky", (0.5, 0.5))}`: the model curve is evaluated at 201 points and splined, cached per temperature
537: Agrees with the constitutional defects as T → 0, the triple defects at the stoichiometric composition obey y_Va = 2 y_anti and exp(−E_triple / 3k_BT), ε_d is recovered from synthetic cells, the builder's curve has no cusp (4 tests, all 57 pass)

557: 6. Equilibrium algorithms without interpolation functions (CALPHAD type)
558: The only CALPHAD-type part of this workflow is the choice of the functions that interpolate between the sample points (ideal mixing + Redlich–Kister, CEF-type sublattices). The phase equilibrium itself is the lower convex hull of stage 06 (common tangent, Eqs. (H1)–(H5)), a procedure that needs no analytic function. Without interpolation functions, the algorithms fall into the following two families.
559: A. Take the equilibrium directly from the sample points without functions (inside 05 → 06). (1) At each temperature, connect the sample points (x_i, G_i ± σ_i) of each phase as they are, or with a smoothing spline weighted by σ. The analytically known terms (ideal mixing (E1), the sublattice s_conf (E10)–(E12)) are exact counting expressions, not CALPHAD, and are kept separate (otherwise the interpolation cannot reproduce the x ln x shape at the end points and sample noise turns into spurious miscibility gaps; Appendix B, section 9, 04A/06). (2) Take the lower convex hull of the point set of all phases. The tangent end points are the sample points themselves, so the boundary resolution is set by the sample spacing, and the error is propagated from σ_i by Monte Carlo. (3) Add sample points near the boundaries and recompute (adaptive sampling). In ftphase this corresponds to builder_from_table(fit="spline" | "smooth"); the price is that sample noise becomes curvature directly, so spurious same-phase intervals appear easily (in practice, intervals that do not move under Monte Carlo are judged to be noise).
560: B. Find the equilibrium directly by simulation without building free-energy curves (replaces 06).
